definitions.explanation: A firmly established habit of doing something, almost always something undesirable or illegal. Most often appears in compounds about repeat offenders.

examples.japanese: {遅刻|ちこく}が{常習|じょうしゅう}になっている。
examples.english: Being late has become a habit.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{万引|まんび}きの{常習|じょうしゅう}{犯|はん}だ。
{無断|むだん}{欠勤|けっきん}が{常習|じょうしゅう}{化|か}し、ついに{解雇|かいこ}された。
examples.english: His unexcused absences became habitual, and he was finally fired.

notes:
{常習|じょうしゅう} refers to an ingrained habit of repeating an action — nearly always negative or criminal. It seldom appears alone, occurring mostly in compounds.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {常習|じょうしゅう}{犯|はん}: habitual offender
- {常習|じょうしゅう}{化|か}する: to become habitual
- {常習|じょうしゅう}{的|てき}: habitual; chronic

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {習慣|しゅうかん}: habit; custom — neutral, can be good or bad
- {癖|くせ}: a personal quirk or habit
